clue.text: Starchy brown bread’s introduced

indicators.note: something introduced is brought in at the front, so this piece goes before the other one

blocks.note: a puri is a puffed, deep-fried Indian bread
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A dull, heavy loaf of brown bread is presented at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Starchy describes the bread on the surface but is the definition: stiff and prim in manner. The bread is introduced in front of the brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Starchy means stiffly formal and prudish, the kind of strict moral rigour associated with a puritan.

clue.text: Little monkey in rabbit hole?

blocks.note: first meaning: a mischievous child, a little rascal
second meaning: a tricky predicament you have fallen into

explanation.surface: A small primate has tumbled down into a burrow.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is a real animal down a hole; both halves are figurative. A child who is a little monkey is also, in British speech, a little pickle, and to be in a pickle is to be stuck in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickle is an affectionate British word for a naughty child, and also means an awkward plight or predicament.

clue.text: Change Turn of the Screw

indicators.note: a turn sends something back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: screw is British prison slang for a warder or jailer

explanation.surface: A call to alter Henry James's famous ghost story, The Turn of the Screw.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic title is the theme of ghost stories, but read literally it says turn the screw: a screw is prison slang for a warder, and WARDER turned round is REDRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw a plan or boundary is to alter or revise it, so it is a verb meaning modify or amend.

clue.text: Tractor crashed into teapots?

definitions.note: a material named for what is made of it: terracotta is the earthenware of pots

indicators.note: a vehicle that has crashed is a mangled wreck, so its letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
the first half of the word, taken as written; its second half is the definition

explanation.surface: A farm vehicle has smashed into a collection of teapots.
explanation.walkthrough: The split is inside a word: teapots is tea, part of the fodder, then pots, the definition. Both of those go into the wreck with TRACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is unglazed brownish-red earthenware, the fired clay used for flowerpots and other vessels.

clue.text: See 19
Juicy thing terror, no mistake, Beloved and The Ring

indicators.note: no means without, so one word is taken away from the other

blocks.note: taken as written
an error is a mistake
angel is a term of endearment for a loved one
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A list of horror titles, Beloved and The Ring, pitched as terror without fault.
explanation.walkthrough: TERROR without ERROR leaves just T. Beloved and The Ring are italic ghost-story titles for the theme, but here they are simply a darling and a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus fruit, a cross between tangerine and pomelo, prized for its sweet, plentiful juice.

clue.text: Other, not the first to drink coffee – but this?

definitions.note: the latter points back to the second of two things, as 'this' does here to coffee

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped
to drink something is to take it inside, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: OTHER without its first letter
a latte is milky espresso coffee

explanation.surface: Offered something else to drink, the speaker asks whether coffee, and this one, is right.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the reflexive 'this?': of the two things named, other and coffee, the second is the latter, and the answer also hides LATTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase the latter refers to the second-mentioned of two items, exactly as a pointing 'this' singles out the last named.

clue.text: What would bring nurse into the school, observing all heads?

definitions.text: What would bring nurse into the school, observing all heads?

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters, and all of them are taken

blocks.note: initials of the four words

explanation.surface: Why the school nurse comes in to inspect every child's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an outbreak of head lice eggs in a British school brings in the so-called nit nurse to check every pupil's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Nits are the eggs of head lice, and their discovery prompts a school health visitor to inspect the pupils' hair.

clue.text: The Sixth Sense and The Others almost like that – it might set one’s heart racing!

definitions.text: it might set one’s heart racing

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

blocks.note: extrasensory perception is often called the sixth sense
the others are the rest
so means in that way

explanation.surface: Two ghost films, The Sixth Sense and The Others, are the sort of thing to make your pulse quicken.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic film titles belong to the ghost-story theme, but are read literally: the sixth sense is ESP, and the others, almost, is RES(t).
explanation.definitionFit: An espresso is a strong shot of coffee, and its caffeine can quicken a drinker's pulse.

clue.text: See 23
Drink: mole caught when in it?

indicators.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it, so a word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a mole is a spy working on the inside, an insider; said out loud that is 'in' plus the drink

explanation.surface: A burrowing mole has fallen into a glass of drink and is caught there.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal is the spy sense of mole. An insider, heard, is someone 'in cider', which is why the clue adds 'when in it': you are only an insider when you are in the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic drink made from fermented apple juice, common in British pubs.

clue.text: Primates discussing a mix of black and white videos?

indicators.note: discussing is talking, so the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

blocks.clueFragment: a mix of black and white videos
blocks.note: black and white mixed make grey; videos are tapes

explanation.surface: Monkeys chatting about old monochrome films.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix black paint with white and you get grey; video cassettes are tapes. Run the two words together and they sound the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The great apes, gorillas, chimpanzees, orangutans and bonobos, are a family within the order of primates.

clue.text: Trick while opening metal container

indicators.note: an opening comes at the start, so this piece sits at the front of what follows

blocks.note: lead is a heavy metal
as can mean while, during the time that
a tray holds things

explanation.surface: A sleight of hand while prising open a tin box.
explanation.walkthrough: The metal comes first in the answer although it is named later; the smaller word opens the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone astray is to deceive or mislead them, steering them wrong by trickery.

clue.text: Sun’s percentage of radioactive gases

indicators.note: a percentage is a portion of a whole, so only part of these words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: How much of the sun is made of radioactive gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Sun means any star here, not ours; the answer runs across radioactiVE GAses.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is one of the brightest stars in the night sky, and every star is a sun to some system.

clue.text: Reformed, I’m a new man in the drinks business

indicators.note: something reformed is remade in a different shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the king is a man in chess

explanation.surface: A former drinker says he has turned over a new leaf and now works with drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Reformed suggests a teetotaller, which makes a drinks job ironic; it is the anagram signal. Man is a chess piece here.
explanation.definitionFit: Making wine from grapes for sale is one branch of the trade that produces alcoholic beverages.

clue.text: Cleaner linen children put on dry

indicators.note: in an across answer, a piece put on another follows right after it

blocks.note: toile is a linen or cotton fabric
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol
issue means offspring

explanation.surface: Laundry instructions: the children's sheets go on to dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry here means teetotal rather than not wet; the children follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet paper is used for wiping, so it serves as something that cleans after using the lavatory.

clue.text: Recovery at the death, crabwise?

blocks.note: at the death is sports slang for in the closing moments
a rally is a recovery or comeback

explanation.surface: A team scrambles back sideways in the closing minutes of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces swap round: the timing, a late phrase in the clue, comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs scuttle sideways, so moving crabwise means moving to the side, which laterally describes.

clue.text: A stick, that’s what I am after – how old can I be?

indicators.note: after means placed behind, so one piece follows another

blocks.note: taken as written
to gel is to stick together, set
I'm contracted
'that's it' and 'that's what' both point at the thing in question

explanation.surface: Someone with a walking stick wonders how long they can go on living.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma matters: 'that's what I am after' is a placing instruction, putting the pronoun after the contraction, not a statement of desire.
explanation.definitionFit: An age limit is the oldest or youngest permitted, the boundary that answers a question about how old one may be.

clue.text: With shot on a field, a region firstly defended – is it?

definitions.text: With shot on a field, a region firstly defended – is it?

indicators.note: in a down answer, one thing on another sits above it, so it comes first
firstly means at the beginning, so only the opening letter is kept
what is defended is surrounded and protected, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a shot is an attempt, a go
taken as written
lea is a poetic word for a meadow
taken as written, the second a
the initial of region

explanation.surface: A footballer shooting on the pitch asks whether this zone is the defended one.
explanation.walkthrough: Lea is a poetic word for meadow that crosswords love. Read whole, the clue also defines: the zone in front of a goal is where shots come from and defenders guard.
explanation.definitionFit: On a football pitch the goal area is the small marked box directly in front of the goal, closely guarded by defenders and keeper.

clue.text: Leader of government has Boris, Rishi and Liz etc for dinner? They’re all dreadful!

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its head, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the initial of government
to have people round for a meal is to host them
Johnson, Sunak and Truss, recent Conservative prime ministers
completes the phrase begun by the verb before the names

explanation.surface: A political joke: a prime minister hosts a dinner for his predecessors, all of them terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: Has … for dinner is one phrase, to host; Tories are members of the British Conservative Party, here its last three prime ministers. Dreadful also means full of dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghost stories are written to frighten, so they are dreadful in the literal sense of inspiring fear and terror.

clue.text: Christian observance very soon put in place in A Christmas Carol

indicators.note: to put something in is to insert it inside another piece

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter
nigh means near, close at hand
to sit something is to place it

explanation.surface: A church observance slotted into Dickens's A Christmas Carol.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make it Dickens's ghost story, in the theme, but read plainly it is a carol sung at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Silent Night is a much-loved hymn sung at Christmas, so it is one example of a festive carol.

clue.text: Fold of skin unknown in identification of fish?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: an eel is a fish
ID is short for identification
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A mysterious flap of skin used to identify a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Identification of fish is the fish followed by its ID; the unknown goes inside the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyelid is the movable flap of skin covering and protecting the eye.

clue.text: Opera ladies and gentlemen heard?

indicators.note: heard means only listened to, so the words count by their sound

blocks.note: the Ladies and the Gents are both public toilets, loos in British slang

explanation.surface: An opera house announcer addresses the audience as ladies and gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: The greeting points at the signs on toilet doors: two loos, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Lulu is the unfinished opera by Alban Berg, first staged in 1937.

clue.text: Meet requirements in advance, the same provided in probe

indicators.note: in puts the pieces inside another

blocks.note: to pry is to probe, poke about
equal means the same
if means provided that

explanation.surface: An inspector checks ahead of time that standards will be met.
explanation.walkthrough: Equal and if, two short words, sit together inside the probing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To prequalify is to be approved as eligible beforehand, satisfying the criteria ahead of a later stage.

clue.text: The Woman in Black, pack leader?

definitions.text: The Woman in Black, pack leader?

blocks.note: surface reading: the Susan Hill ghost story, in italics
setter's reading: a black-suited lady who ranks high among playing cards

explanation.walkthrough: The italic title steers to the novel and film, but a woman in black in a pack of cards is a royal card of a black suit; Pushkin wrote a ghost story of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: This court card is a female figure in a dark suit, outranked in the deck only by king and ace.

clue.text: Measure force and energy

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police force
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A physics instruction to measure both force and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Force sounds like physics, but it is a police force; the Met is London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete is an old verb for measuring out or allotting, surviving in the phrase mete out punishment.

clue.text: European city, one featured by magazine from another world?

indicators.note: whatever is featured by something is carried within its pages

blocks.note: Mars is another planet
Elle is a fashion magazine
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A city profiled in an alien magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The magazine comes from another world, so MARS goes in front of it; one sits inside the magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Marseille is France's great Mediterranean port, its second-largest settlement.

clue.text: Copybook baldie blotted after shaving of bonce

indicators.note: shaving takes the hair off the top, so the head letter is removed
a blotted page is smudged into a mess, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: baldie without its first letter, the head of bonce
bonce is British slang for head; its first letter is the one shaved off

explanation.surface: A bald man's exercise book has been splodged with ink after he shaved his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Blotting your copybook is spoiling a perfect record, so the clue's first and third words echo the idiom. Bonce is slang for head.
explanation.definitionFit: Copybook as an adjective means exemplary or textbook-perfect, like the model handwriting in a school copybook.

clue.text: Dark Matter seemingly invisible to youth in test

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

blocks.note: a try is a test or attempt
elderly people often feel unseen by the young

explanation.surface: Michelle Paver's ghost story Dark Matter, apparently unnoticed by young readers taking an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic title belongs to the ghost-story theme, but as a definition it is plain: a dark matter, a grim subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a grim, sorrowful event or drama, so a dark matter in the sense of a sombre subject.

clue.text: Arm in difficulty, squashed

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: need is hardship, difficulty
gat is old slang for a gun, a firearm

explanation.surface: An arm trapped in a tight spot and crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: Arm is a weapon, not a limb: GAT is gangster slang for a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: Negated means nullified or cancelled out, as an objection is squashed or quashed.
